entry.title: How to find the missing helmet in ARC Raiders – Keeping the Memory walkthrough
entry.summary:
If you have been enjoying the search missions in ARC Raiders, Keeping the Memory will make you don your investigative hats once more.
This quest is obtained from Celeste and is quite simple to complete. However, the location of the quest item can be pretty confusing for some. This guide will help you finish the quest and obtain the rewards.
Table of contents ARC Raiders Keeping the Memory walkthrough ARC Raiders Keeping the Memory rewards
ARC Raiders Keeping the Memory walkthrough
The Keeping the Memory quest can be broken down into three parts.
Reach the wreckage in the Formicai Hills
Search for the missing helmet
Return the helmet to the memorial
To complete the quest, we will have to visit Dam Battlegrounds. The wreckage is near the Scrap Yard, where there is a wreckage of a gigantic spider-shaped ARC on the ground. You'll have to find a helmet at this location.
Screenshot and Remix by Destructoid
The helmet is hidden in front of a small scrub and behind a small stone. The scrub is located near a big tree close to the ARC itself. Once you get near the scrub, aim down, and the quest will update, hinting at the location of the helmet. This area typically doesn't have any ARC enemies, so you can finish the task pretty quickly.
Pick the helmet up and speak with Celeste after returning to Speranza to complete Keeping the Memory.
ARC Raiders Keeping the Memory rewards
Here are all the rewards you get from completing the Keeping the Memory quest.
5 Simple Gun Parts
5 Duct Tape
5 Magnet
In many ways, the Keeping the Memory quest is easier compared to the likes of Medical Merchandise and Reduced to Rubble, where the tasks are more confusing. If you're focusing solely on the quests, make sure to matchmake with a free loadout to reduce the chances of losing any valuable resource upon death.

entry.title: How to complete Market Correction quest in ARC Raiders
entry.summary:
Market Correction is one of many "search and find" missions you get from Tian Wen in ARC Raiders, and it can become a bit of a headspinner.
In the Market Correction quest, you're tasked with locating a cache and sabotaging it to finish the job. This guide will lay out all the essential steps to complete this quest and get your deserved rewards.
Table of contents ARC Raiders Market Correction quest walkthrough ARC Raiders Market Correction quest rewards
ARC Raiders Market Correction quest walkthrough
The Market Correction quest will require us to travel to the Outskirts region in Buried City. To be more precise, you'll need to reach the Marano Station, which is located in the western part of the Buried City. I have marked the location to make it easier for you to find the correct place on the map.
Screenshot and Remix by Destructoid
Incidentally, the "cache" in this mission isn't actually a cache like the ones we found in the Marked for Death quest. Instead, it's a pair of dustbins that you have to find and sabotage. The dustbins are located in the northern part of Marano Station. If you're at the marked location, you'll find a bunker-type structure. Go to the rear of the building, and you'll find the dustbins. Once you interact with them, wait for a few seconds for the quest to update.
Once the quest updates, interact with the bins one more time to complete the sabotage. This will complete the quest, and you'll get your rewards from Tian Wen.
ARC Raiders Market Correction quest rewards
The Market Correction quest grants you the following rewards.
Silencer II
Extended Light Mag I
Compensator I
It's a neat set of rewards for the amount of work that needs to be done. If you're looking to complete more quests, both Medical Merchandise and Straight Record are excellent options.

entry.title: Where is Bilguun’s Hideout located in ARC Raiders
entry.summary:
The Bilguun's Hideout location in ARC Raiders is a vital quest area, but finding the place can be really challenging if you don't know where to look.
This location is tied with the What We Left Behind quest in Spaceport. The quest requires you to find rare loot in three spots on the Spaceport map. This guide will help you find the location if you have yet to find it.
Bilguun's Hideout location in ARC Raiders
The first task is to enter Spaceport. Unlocking the map requires a fair amount of time as you proceed through the earlier locations. Once done, you'll want to move to the central part of the map. Bilguun's Hideout is located right next to the Container Storage building. I have marked the spot on the screenshot below for your convenience.
Screenshot and Remix by Destructoid
Bilguun's Hideout is a small container that's attached to the wall that serves as the boundary for Container Storage. When you approach the spot, you'll want to tread carefully. Stick close to the wall to protect yourself from enemy fire. While I haven't found too many ARCs, the location always attracts human players since it's tied to the quest.
There's a ladder that leads you into the container. I didn't find any loot at the location, but the quest item is a bunch of notes. Once you find the notes, the objective will automatically update, and it will automatically bring up the What We Left Behind quest.
Bilguun's Hideout should be the third and last task to complete as part of the quest. Your first objective will be to find a set of notes in the South Swamp Outpost area of Dam Battlegrounds. This will be followed by going to the Parking Garage in Buried City.
Once you loot any two containers in the Parking Garage, you'll be tasked with heading over to Bilguun's Hideout and finding the valuable loot (the notes).

entry.title: The hardest part of making Arc Raiders was creating a "meaningful" item meta so that your loot doesn't just feel like "cash"
entry.summary:
A question I often ask game developers when I've run out of real questions is: what was the hardest part of making your game? Which is a terrible line of inquiry, because it's like asking somebody with their foot in a hornet's nest which individual hornet they dislike the most. As Arc Raiders executive producer Aleksander Grøndal told me in a chat last week, "I can probably sit here and talk to you about all the problems we've had for hours on end, but yeah, game development is always tricky. That's what I can say. There's nothing that comes for free - everything is a constant struggle."
Still, the question often gets an interesting response, because as readers of Alex Wiltshire's old The Mechanic series will know, big problems may necessitate inventive solutions. So, what has been the hardest part of making Arc Raiders? Perfecting the slides? Avoiding mandatory player progression resets from season to season? Dealing with reports about the game's generative AI usage? According to Grøndal, it was trying to create an economy of loot and crafting materials - ranging from all-purpose Mechanical Components to rare or uncommon ingredients for specific guns, sometimes found in special field depots - that isn't too "punishing" and which doesn't just feel like accumulating "cash value".

entry.title: Arc Raiders doesn't AI-generate guns from Youtube videos, Embark clarifies: "that's a research project, and not something that we're using in the game now"
entry.summary:
Let's get the hot potato out of the way without preamble: Embark's extraction shooter Arc Raiders doesn't include any gun models generated from Youtube videos, executive producer Aleksander Grøndal has told RPS in an interview about the game's usage of generative AI and machine learning technologies.
This clarification follows the partial online publication of an Edge magazine interview in which Embark CEO Patrick Söderlund made various claims for the studio's in-house tech, including the suggestion that the developers "can take a video from YouTube, feed it through our tools and pipelines, and [produce] a 3D model of the weapon you had in that video." According to Grøndal, this particular technology is not actually used in Arc Raiders. "That's a research project, and that's not something that we're using in the game now," he told me over a video call this Monday, following a sprawling and generally enjoyable hands-on.

entry.title: Audio recenze: Černý telefon 2 [Black Phone 2] - 50 %
entry.summary: První díl sice měl naprosto nesmyslný náhodný děj, ale docela působivou retro atmosféru. entry.title: Audio recenze: Pohled do slunce [In die Sonne schauen] - 40 %
entry.summary: "Pocitový" film s dobře fungující atmosférou a výbornými herci, kterému podráží nohy extrémní délka a extrémní pomalost všeho, co se v něm děje. Při třetím pomalém švenkování po stejné černobílé fotografii jsem zažíval téměř psychoteror a po 90 minutách jsem vážně uvažoval, že odejdu ze sálu. Námět je v mnoha ohledech podobný filmu "Hodiny" (2002), takže pokud vám ten připadal příliš komerční a přímočarý, "Pohled do slunce" zahraje na vaši artovou notu. (Ilča 40 %)

entry.title: Audio recenze: Fichtelberg - 30 %
entry.summary: Potenciálně zajímavý námět, který bohužel shazuje špatný scénář, špatná režie a špatné skoro všechno ostatní. Ne tak úžasně špatné jako třeba "Kněžna Libuše", ale jenom "špatné" ve smyslu "nekvalitní a nezajímavé". Dlouho jsem nezažil, aby se mi 90 minut v kině takhle hrozně vleklo. Je to škoda, protože základní myšlenka byla zajímavá a herci se snažili. Specificky bych zdůraznil extrémně odbytou hudbu ve chvílích, které si přímo říkaly o silné hudební motivy. (Ilča 20 %)
